title: New London-Waterford Speedbowl

services.name: The Speedbowl
services.desc: The New London-Waterford Speedbowl opened on April 15, 1951 as a 1/3 mile crushed blue stone oval race track. Its ownership group, The New London-Waterford Speedbowl, Inc., was composed of 6 local businessmen. The original headlining division were Modified stock cars, called Sportsmen Stocks at the time. The first event winner was Bob Swift. After 3 weeks of operation, the dust created during green flag segments of racing became a nuisance to spectators. The track closed for about a month and re-opened as an asphalt oval, which it remains today. blurb: For immediate release from the New London-Waterford Speedbowl WATERFORD - Keith Rocco pulled Adam Gada at the Start of the SK Modifieds®, but rather than run away with it, Gada closed the gap and stayed there. Not long after and under attack by Anthony Flannery, Rocco’s lead would increase. Flannery poked outside a couple times but eventual contact between the two sent Gada around just short of halfway.
